name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before any human review. It catches 80% of trivial issues—linting, test coverage gaps, and style violations—freeing humans to focus on design and intent. The trade-off is slower feedback for developers who prefer instant merges, but the quality gain outweighs the delay.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 80% catch rate normalizes mediocrity by teaching teams to accept "objective" issues like test coverage gaps as the baseline—it doesn’t measure real impact. The real risk isn’t slower PRs; it’s that developers stop questioning *why* those issues matter, turning quality into a checkbox ritual. Settle it by tracking whether the issues PR-Agent flags actually reduce bugs or regressions in production, not just merge speed.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: PR-Agent’s 80% catch rate risks training teams to treat symptoms—like missing tests—not causes. The real risk is that developers stop asking *why* coverage gaps exist, turning quality into a bureaucratic hurdle instead of a design constraint. A better alternative: run PR-Agent *after* human review to flag *only* the issues that actually block decisions, not the ones that just slow merges. Settle it by measuring whether PR-Agent’s output changes the *kind* of bugs that reach production, not just the count of trivial violations.
